Drizzt and Belwar range out from Blingdenstone and meet Clacker, a pech cursed by a wizard into the body of a hook horror, who keeps his own mind but loses a little of it to the beast every time he fights. The three travel together. Drizzt is captured by mind flayers, whose mental domination strips away his will entirely and leaves him a compliant slave in their enclave; Belwar and Clacker break in and get him out, and the rescue costs them. In the city, the house war ends: House Do'Urden destroys House Hun'ett and Malice kills SiNafay herself. It is a decisive victory that changes nothing, because the Spider Queen still will not answer her while Drizzt lives.

Out of options, Matron Malice petitions the Spider Queen and is granted Zin-carla, the highest favor the goddess bestows: the corpse of Zaknafein, animated and guided by the matron's own will, given back his skill with two blades and set on Drizzt's trail. The spirit-wraith is tireless, needs neither food nor rest, and cannot be reasoned with. Word of what is coming reaches Drizzt, who understands immediately what it means for anyone standing near him. He refuses to let Blingdenstone be destroyed on his account and leaves the gnome city; Belwar refuses to let him leave alone, and Clacker goes with them.

The three are hunted through the tunnels without pause. Drizzt cannot outrun the wraith and cannot bring himself to destroy the body of the father who died for him, and every encounter goes badly. Clacker's curse has been advancing throughout the chase, and he knows how little of himself is left; he turns and fights the wraith to buy the others distance, and is killed. Drizzt is left facing the certainty that he must confront Zaknafein's remains himself, on ground of his own choosing, and that his mother is watching through the thing's eyes.

In the final confrontation Drizzt fights the spirit-wraith while talking to his father, refusing to treat the thing as merely an enemy. Zaknafein's own will breaks through Matron Malice's control long enough for him to end the animated body himself rather than be turned against his son. Zin-carla fails. The Spider Queen, denied twice, withdraws from Malice altogether and transforms her into a drider, and House Do'Urden is left in ruins. Drizzt is alive and free of the immediate hunt, but he accepts that wherever he settles in the Underdark will become a target, and that Blingdenstone has already paid enough for taking him in. He refuses the deep gnomes' offer of a home, says goodbye to Belwar, and turns toward the tunnels leading up, meaning to try the surface world he saw only once.

characters.description: A Founder leading a refugee caravan west in search of a free home in the Shiverglades. Hal combines costly Founder abilities with volatile Beastborn magic, and his determination to protect the caravan repeatedly puts him at personal risk.
characters.name: Hal

characters.description: A Sin Keeper traveling with Hal's party who begins bleeding severely from Broken Faith. Ordinary healing cannot cure the condition, leaving her in immediate danger as Hal enters her mind to investigate its cause.
characters.name: Ashera

characters.description: A protective ranger traveling with Hal's party. Elora is pursuing a strange quest tied to a sound only she can hear, even as she works to keep the badly injured Ashera alive during the group's westward journey.
characters.name: Elora

characters.description: A former Reaper who has recently become mortal and no longer has the directives that once defined her existence. She is tied to Hal and enters this story searching for a purpose, a community, and a way to understand her new life.
characters.name: Noth

characters.description: A highly skilled aerial and close-quarters fighter accompanying Hal's caravan. Mira supports the opening battle, helps pursue Elora's quest, and shows signs that she is withholding something about the quest prompt.
characters.name: Mira

characters.description: A member of Hal's westbound party who fights alongside Hal, Mira, Elora, and Ashera against giant noxus on the Felton Plains.
characters.name: Angram

characters.description: A ruling Founder whose willingness to abuse control troubles Hal. His distant authority threatens the caravan's pursuit of freedom.
characters.name: Rinbast

characters.description: A mysterious figure named by the quest that guides Elora's party toward a heart-shaped lake. Mira knows more about the wording of that quest than she admits, leaving Komachi's nature and connection to Elora initially uncertain.
characters.name: Komachi

characters.description: An oracle associated with a route through the Crystal Groves and Mirror Lands that could provide the caravan with needed supplies.
characters.name: Luda

characters.description: A dwarf associated with Clan Bouldergut, whose durable equipment supplies Hal's group.
characters.name: Durvin

characters.description: An intelligent mimic bonded to Hal as family. Vorax carries extradimensional storage, travels with his slime companion Quibbles, and protects Hal with a loyalty that extends beyond ordinary ownership or service.
characters.name: Vorax

characters.description: Vorax's pet slime, carried within one of the mimic's extradimensional stomachs.
characters.name: Quibbles

characters.description: A gnome ally traveling with Hal's caravan.
characters.name: Rondo

characters.description: A blue-feathered carrick fitted with armor and weapons who insists on joining Hal's scouting expedition.
characters.name: Blue-feathered carrick

characters.description: The dangerous inner counterpart bound to Hal's Beastborn class. Hal believes Besal will exploit weakness to escape and threaten his friends, making every increase in Beastborn power a struggle over control as well as survival.
characters.name: Besal

characters.description: A caravan ranger whose knowledge of the Mirror Lands helps the travelers avoid concealed chasms and other hidden hazards.
characters.name: Yesel

characters.description: The local leader who orders her scouts to test Hal's caravan instead of destroying the intruders. She believes her people must adapt to changing dangers and uses a controlled trial to judge whether the newcomers might alter their fate.
characters.name: Ebon Star war leader

characters.description: A local scout leader who questions the war leader's departure from tradition, then follows her order to shadow Hal's caravan.
characters.name: Ebon Star scout leader

characters.description: An intelligent gold-scaled dragon who commands the keens within a warded mountain complex. He meets Vorax in a book-filled chamber and says he has been expecting him, though his intentions are not yet known.
characters.name: Gold dragon

characters.description: A wounded wild creature spared by Hal after a battle between monster families. It remains nearby without attacking him, though it is not yet an established companion.
characters.name: Rhinoceros beetle

characters.description: The rhinoceros beetle that remained near Hal during his isolation in the Shiverglades. After tending his fire and accompanying him through dangerous territory without hostility, the creature receives the simple name Beetle.
characters.name: Beetle

characters.description: A hostile survivor of an ancient marked order, encountered in sealed ruins beneath a temple. He bears a copper-colored mark related to Hal's and tries to seize Hal's superior mark after identifying himself as one of his order's last members.
characters.name: Copper mage

characters.description: A discorporated member of the ancient council who covertly approaches Hal in the abyss. Acting at another council member's request, he warns that the awakened mages may use Hal in their internal conflict and offers help toward an exit.
characters.name: Iron mage

characters.description: A scarred alternate version of Hal who bears a dark branded mark. He mirrors Hal's magic, calls Hal a renegade, and attacks with the practiced knowledge of someone who shares Hal's fundamental nature.
characters.name: Kinslayer 36

recaps.ending: At dawn, the void mist burns away and the surviving attackers are killed or driven off. Bravers Guild wins its first Shiverglades incursion and receives a 48-hour Home and Hearth benefit that recognizes its settlement claim. Hal survives injured and reunites with Noth. Besal voluntarily returns control after helping defeat Rinbast's scarred counterpart, and their three Communions leave them as willing partners with deeper access to one another's memories and power. Hal inherits the dead counterpart's soul and abilities and has promised to free the other counterparts held by Rinbast. The victory does not restore everyone. Komachi's frightened burst has removed Ashera, Elora, Durvin, Vorax, and more than a dozen defenders to an unknown place. Noth intends to organize the search. Mira is alive after spending the gold dragon's scale power, though her instability within Aldim remains unresolved. The settlement has only a brief period to recover and repair, while the foreign Copper Coaltheel, the ancient council, Rinbast, and future Shiverglades attacks remain open threats.
recaps.in_short: Hal leads a refugee caravan into the Shiverglades to found a free settlement beyond Rinbast's control. He saves Ashera from Broken Faith, establishes Bravers Guild, secures a monoseed, and plants it as a mana tree that anchors the new refuge and ties both Hal and Noth to its survival. Local allies, a trapped gold dragon, and the guild's combined labor help prepare for the region's first assault. During a separate quest, Hal completes three Dark Communions with Besal and attracts the attention of an ancient Coaltheel council. The settlement survives a void-driven siege, but Komachi teleports Ashera, Elora, Durvin, Vorax, and other defenders to an unknown destination. Hal and Besal defeat Rinbast's void-corrupted scarred counterpart, with Besal rejecting ascension and choosing Hal as his brother. Dawn ends the incursion, leaving the guild with a temporary claim, missing friends to recover, and Hal's promise to free Rinbast's other captive counterparts.

recaps.text: Previously: Hal became a Founder in Aldim and gathered companions while resisting the rule of Rinbast. His Beastborn class gave him powerful monster-derived magic but also bound him to Besal, a dangerous inner counterpart capable of contesting control. Hal's choices also transformed Noth from a Reaper into a mortal woman, leaving her without the directives and certainty that once defined her. Vorax, an intelligent mimic, became part of Hal's chosen family. By the beginning of this volume, Hal is leading refugees west toward the Shiverglades, where he hopes to establish a free sanctuary for people unwilling to live under Rinbast. The caravan includes fighters, dwarves, koblins, and other allies who have placed their future in Hal's hands. Their goal is not merely escape. They need a defensible home, supplies, and a source of power strong enough to sustain an independent community.

Hal's party travels west while helping Elora follow a quest only she can hear. Ashera nearly dies from Broken Faith, the punishment imposed after she opposed Rinbast and lost access to her Sinkeeper healing. Hal enters her mind with Dominate and breaks the restraints causing the bleeding, but the rescue places his Founder mark on her and creates an unwanted awareness link. He later dismisses active control and keeps the circumstances private until Ashera admits to the group that she can no longer heal. Her companions refuse to abandon her. A flock of corrupted creatures nearly kills Mira and forces Hal to spend almost all his experience dominating attackers and using them to restore the party. At the heart-shaped lake, Elora crosses alone to a ruined island, defeats corrupted spirits, and meets Komachi, a small speaking Pobol. Elora accepts a fabled Wilds Master evolution and forms a permanent familiar pact with Komachi, whose unusual magic includes travel to a Feyworld and an ability to locate treasure.

Komachi retrieves a huge locked coffer and joins the caravan with Elora. Vorax senses that the new familiar conceals immense power, but accepts her friendship after finding no malicious intent. Ashera withdraws from combat and becomes quartermaster and alchemy teacher, though the loss of her former role continues to distress her. Hal learns to make a potent but toxic emergency health injection. Noth, struggling with mortality, tells Hal that she once blamed him for her condition but now recognizes her own choices in the change. She forgives him, returns to his immediate group, and begins defining a life built around home, friendship, and chosen purpose. Komachi grants Hal's wagon group a temporary skill-learning blessing, which Hal, Ashera, and Noth use for intensive alchemy practice. Rondo explains the Boulderguts' valuable mineral customs and their growing respect for Hal. As the training ends, Yesel reports a rapidly approaching monostorm, and Hal orders the caravan into a tight defensive formation.

Luda amplifies Hal's Monoshields until they cover the caravan, but fighters must still meet the monostorm's crystalline creatures outside the protection. Hal confronts Ashera's belief that she has become useless and swears an Oath of Compassion to restore or replace her lost magic. She returns to the front line and proves she can still provide powerful combat support. As the storm evolves, Hal identifies a distortion at its center. His companions clear a path, and Mira carries him through the caustic air before turning back. Touching the distortion ends the immediate storm but sends Hal to a separate arena against its enormous guardian. He refuses to surrender control to Besal, survives severe strain, and uses improvised bone weapons after the guardian destroys his sword. Hal shatters the creature's exposed chest jewel and kills it, earning valuable storm materials and a title. The collapsing arena then drops him from a great height, but he fashions a membrane parachute and returns alive, injured and suffering potion toxicity.

Ashera treats Hal's toxicity while Besal offers a more cooperative relationship, claiming Beastborn and counterpart should function symbiotically. Hal remains wary. He improves his leadership abilities and resumes the journey toward the Lone Arch, where the caravan expects to find a mana seed. Hal enters the warded arch realm alone and follows strict rules that forbid weapons, magic, and hostile intent. After navigating its shifting paths, he takes a living monoseed from a dying tree and survives the realm's violent rejection. Durvin explains that the seed can establish a true guild before it is planted without preventing its eventual use for a settlement. Hal creates Bravers Guild and becomes guildmaster. Noth is the first to join, followed by Hal's trusted companions and then the wider caravan. Durvin's acceptance brings Clan Bouldergut into the guild, while Vorax becomes treasurer and the koblins receive advisory standing. The new guild has members and a portable bank, but no territory, archetype, or permanent home.

The guild encounters an abandoned human caravan whose intelligent carracks have survived independently. After Hal's group treats their wounded young, Komachi translates their account and helps secure an agreement under which they join as friends rather than property. A diary reveals their former humans were pursuing Rinbast's bounty on Hal. Noth tells Hal she wants to fight and explore beside him after the sanctuary is safe, and their growing attraction remains unresolved. Hal develops a formal Bonecraft discipline while creating Emissary, a fabled bone falchion that stores mana and can return to him across miles. Rediscovering Bonecraft raises Bravers Guild to level one. Hal centralizes supplies in the guild bank, selects an Authority perk for operational information, and turns exceptional meals for Komachi into the guild's first quest. Fed by competing cooks, Komachi accelerates the lighter caravan. The group leaves the Mirror Lands, crosses dangerous country, and reaches the Barrier Peaks one day from the Shiverglades.

Hal continues developing Bonecraft and portable mana storage while preparing the caravan's future fighters and leaders. At Fool's Pass, a projection delivers Rinbast's offer: abandon the rebellion and Hal may return to Earth or leave for another world. Hal refuses because acceptance would mean betraying his companions. Inside the Shiverglades, the caravan meets the Ebon Star tribe through a controlled trial. After Hal and Noth defeat a fog beast, the tribe provides umbral branches that repel the Void Mist and assigns a suspicious scout leader to guide the outsiders. She leads the caravan safely toward the central mountain. Hal rejects several possible sites until Noth and Yesel find a sheltered valley with water, natural barriers, and access into the mountain. Komachi plants the monoseed there. It rapidly becomes a protective mana tree whose influence improves recovery and suppresses harmful area effects. Hal accepts guardianship and a soul tether that makes the tree his resurrection point.

Planting the monoseed begins a claim trial: the settlement must survive an assault in seven days while preserving both the tree and most of its people. Hal assigns gathering, surveying, construction, and monster diplomacy across the guild. Bravers Guild adopts the Settlement archetype and converts from a caravan into an outpost, gaining a temporary Founder's Day advantage. Hal binds the settlement to the mana tree, making their survival inseparable. Durvin's measurements show that sealing the valley entrance will require extensive walls and more material than the guild possesses, so Hal and Noth consider mass-produced bone construction. Meanwhile Vorax and the koblins explore the mountain opening and discover a warded society of bat-like scouts led by a trapped gold dragon. The dragon welcomes the new settlement, offers his scouts and advice, and warns that the Shiverglades will attack it. He also confirms that the mana-tree bond makes Hal and Noth effectively immortal as long as the tree survives.

The gold dragon offers reconnaissance and selected planning knowledge but cannot leave his confinement to fight. Hal delegates construction and uses the mana tree's influence to cultivate possible plant allies around it. Elora develops warming equipment for Komachi and the wider settlement. Local observers recognize Komachi as a rare ancient being and debate whether Hal's community can survive the coming regional response. The settlement struggles to balance food, shelter, walls, and morale within its seven-day deadline. Luda identifies useful specialists among her followers, including a chef and construction workers, while Hal improves wall projects and designs trap-focused defenses. The planted creatures transform under the mana tree, whose rapid growth and emotional connection convince Hal to protect it from exploitation. Luda then links her oracle amplification to the tree and extends Founder's Day to cover the entire defense window. The settlement retains its crucial bonuses to morale, production, gathering, recovery, and learning through the expected night of attack.

Hal converts ordinary building components into reproducible bone bricks and palisade spikes, then joins Noth in Durvin's Ironspine construction band. His Bonecraft abilities sharply reduce costs and accelerate the defenses. The guild completes enough work to advance from outpost to encampment, unlocking specialized buildings and research. Noth affirms that mortality has given her the home and happiness she lacked as a Reaper. Elora leaves with the Ebon Star guide to seek missing scouts and possible help, learning that Komachi's species predates Aldim's world-shard rules and follows them by choice. The guide says such beings are god-like but not divine. Back at the settlement, organized meals and warming equipment improve daily life while wall construction moves ahead of schedule. The town hall is completed, and Hal designates it as a recreation space to protect morale even though this reduces workforce efficiency. The refuge now has a communal center and stronger defenses, but repeated monster activity shows the surrounding danger is already increasing.

Hal and Noth kill a powerful vine creature near the works, then acknowledge their feelings and begin a romantic relationship. Repeated attacks lead Hal to form a scouting party with Noth, Ashera, Angram, Durvin, and an armed carrack. Angram receives authority over the settlement's rangers, and Ashera returns to active protection despite her unresolved loss of magic. Outside the valley, the party finds that Void Mist recoils from Hal because of his link to the mana tree. Organized mantis-like creatures ambush them. The group defeats the first wave, but an abnormal survivor molts into a much larger leader, paralyzes the party, and gravely injures the carrack. Hal accepts limited power from Besal while Noth turns the enemy's spilled blood into healing for the group. Hal and Durvin sever the leader's rear legs, but it takes flight with Hal clinging to its body. He is carried away from his companions with little mana and no immediate route back.

Hal kills the flying leader in midair and survives the resulting fall, but lands alone far from the settlement. Reaching Beastborn level twenty gives him stronger essence combinations and a class quest centered on Besal. The counterpart manifests face to face, apologizes for his earlier attempts at control, and proposes a dangerous cooperative ritual. Hal must choose between purging Besal and completing three Dark Communions. He chooses communion in hopes of gaining enough synchronization to prevent future loss of control. Besal guides him to a mana-rich conflict between monster families, where Hal tests new abilities and spares a wounded rhinoceros beetle. The first Communion traps Hal in a false version of his old life on Earth, offering familiar misery at the price of forgetting Aldim and his companions. Besal helps him recognize the illusion. Hal rejects the retreat, breaks free with Besal, and completes the first trial. He establishes a temporary camp, still separated from his party, with two Communions remaining.

The spared beetle tends Hal's camp while he crafts insulated replacement armor from several monster essences. His new synchronization allows Besal to lend mana and briefly manifest outside Hal, so Hal equips him with a bone sword. Bat messengers report that Noth's party is safe but unwilling to abandon the search. Hal and Noth agree that she will return to direct the settlement defenses while he continues his class quest. Traveling with Besal and the beetle, Hal causes an uncontrolled forest fire while testing enhanced explosive magic, then crosses a region filled with strange ancient structures linked to his Founder mark. His map stops identifying the area. The trio enters vast ruins beyond a protected boundary, where an unnatural calm masks a history of severe conflict. Besal believes the site contains the conditions needed for the second Communion, but warns Hal that the peace itself is part of the danger.

Within the ruins, Hal activates a temple dais and descends into a cavern where a copper-marked ancient mage tries to steal his Founder mark. The mage merges with a massive void creature, forcing Hal and manifested Besal into a desperate fight. Hal collapses the platform beneath the enemy, and Besal saves him during the fall. Hal seizes the mage's Copper Coaltheel as the attacker dies, then awakens before a council of thirteen discorporated mages. The council rules that he acted in defense but leaves him to escape the abyss without aid. An iron mage covertly guides him out and warns that the awakened council may draw Hal into its internal struggle. Three days have passed. Hal immediately completes his second Communion with Besal, freeing them both from illusions that exploit their fears and desire for power. He names the accompanying rhinoceros beetle Beetle and races home carrying the foreign Copper Coaltheel, whose continuing bleed drains and injures him.

Hal advances his magic and begins the long return to the settlement, expecting to arrive after the attack starts. During his absence, Noth becomes acting leader. She resolves labor disputes, works with Ashera and the dwarves, and orders defensive tunnels and elevated positions cut into the cliffs around the valley gap. Durvin recognizes that Clan Bouldergut now regards the refuge as home and trusts both Hal's vision and Noth's command. Elsewhere in the mountain, Mira reveals to the gold dragon that she entered Aldim improperly and is being rejected by the world shard. The dragon temporarily stabilizes her and gives her a single-use gold scale for emergency power, agreeing to conceal her condition. At the wall, Durvin oversees layered traps and preparations for Elora's hoped-for return. The expected siege begins early when monsters erupt from the ground inside the gap, and defenders rush to the high ground while Hal remains absent.

Hal develops short-burst flight, dominates a powerful feline as a mount, and reaches the settlement during the mass assault. Noth has already organized parapets, catapults, ranger positions, and cliff defenses. Ashera runs triage, potions, supplies, messengers, and rest rotations, while Durvin commands the wall. Hal uses the mana tree's defensive power, recruits a transformed tree ant, and attacks the horde from above to create fire lanes for repairs. A black miasma then suppresses light and drives the mana barrier inward. Hal's miniature-sun sigil reveals that Void Mist is reanimating and directing dead monsters. The sigil's backlash incapacitates his body, but his mind remains active through creatures he has dominated. He turns them against the horde, repairs walls, and crystallizes defenses through his new mark abilities. With his controlled force dwindling and the wall certain to fail under sustained pressure, Hal sends the tree ant away and commits to a final plan whose result remains unknown.

Elora returns with the Ebon Star scout leader and roughly two dozen local fighters, who treat the void corruption as a threat to their own homeland. The reinforcements learn that Hal's marked monsters are allies and help shore up the wall. Ashera uses increasingly dangerous occult and spell-seizing magic to clear attackers and rescue Durvin outside the defenses. A redirected destructive spell still detonates near her. The blast vaporizes part of the wall, opens an eastern breach, and leaves Ashera, Durvin, and other defenders badly injured. Elora breaks her leg trying to reach Ashera. Komachi reacts in terror, first driving nearby monsters into a frenzy and then releasing a prismatic burst. Elora, Ashera, Durvin, Vorax, and at least a dozen other people vanish. Their destination and condition are unknown. The injured scout leader uses her greatsword and duplicating magic to hold the breach while Luda sustains a failing barrier. The settlement survives for the moment, but the defense has lost several of its central leaders.

Mira spends the gold dragon's scale power to break the magic suppressing Hal's consciousness, then joins the breach defense with strength from another world shard. A hooded, scarred attacker who resembles Hal intercepts her. Hal awakens without access to his mark abilities and takes over the duel, discovering that the enemy mirrors his Beastborn spells and combat knowledge. The attacker is a scarred alternate Hal branded and controlled by Rinbast. Besal blocks a killing blow, allowing Hal to keep fighting despite severe wounds. The counterpart explains that Rinbast's control is absolute and resents Hal for escaping it. Hal drains his opponent's strain, entering increasingly dangerous states as both versions exchange opposing essence combinations. When Hal detonates magic inside an existing chest wound, he disrupts the power that had contained the corruption there. The wound becomes a black-hole heart that consumes spells and transforms the counterpart into a void-racked creature, renewing the fight under far more dangerous conditions.

Hal and Besal share control to keep the void-racked counterpart away from the settlement, but the enemy's black-hole heart turns the duel into attrition. They use mana-tree energy to reflect void lightning and weaken the corruption. The heart eventually pulls Hal out of Besal and traps him inside, where he defeats a copying manifestation by exploiting its inability to create anything new. Besal reaches the final strain threshold but rejects ascension into a star-bound horror, choosing instead to save Hal. The dying counterpart asks Hal to end his life before the corruption erases him and reveals that other branded brothers remain under Rinbast's control. Hal promises to free them and kills him. Hal then reunites with Besal, completing their third Communion in substance as Besal voluntarily returns control and names Hal his friend and brother. Dawn burns away the Void Mist and ends the incursion. Bravers Guild receives a temporary recognized claim, but Ashera, Elora, Durvin, Vorax, and the others taken by Komachi remain missing. Noth commits the survivors to finding them.

characters.description: Returning from Milu with proof of GrayCris's illegal salvage operation, the SecUnit is traveling under a false identity toward Preservation to deliver the evidence to Dr. Mensah in person. It is out of practice at being near people it cares about, still passing as an augmented human whenever it has to, and about to discover that its plan has been overtaken by events.
characters.name: Murderbot

characters.description: The leader of the survey team the SecUnit once guarded, a planetary administrator of Preservation Alliance and the legal holder of the SecUnit's contract, a technicality she keeps only to protect it. She has spent the time since the survey fighting GrayCris in arbitration over what the company did on that planet, which has made her its most expensive problem.
characters.name: Dr. Ayda Mensah

characters.description: The survey team's lawyer, now running the legal fight against GrayCris. Blunt, formidable, and not remotely intimidated by corporate security or by the fact that she is operating on a company-owned station.
characters.name: Pin-Lee

characters.description: A member of the old survey team, delighted to see the SecUnit again and entirely willing to say so out loud, which the SecUnit finds harder to cope with than being shot at.
characters.name: Dr. Ratthi

characters.description: The augmented human from the survey team, still watchful of the SecUnit and still the fastest of the group inside the feed, which makes him valuable in a place where every system belongs to the other side.
characters.name: Dr. Gurathin

characters.description: A military-grade security construct deployed by the station's corporate security against the SecUnit: larger, faster and far better armed than a standard unit, and operating under full external control with none of the SecUnit's freedom or hesitation. It is the most dangerous opponent the SecUnit has faced.
characters.name: The Combat SecUnit

recaps.ending: Mensah is freed and GrayCris's last attempt at leverage fails: the company is exposed at TranRollinHyfa, and with the arbitration already lost, it has nothing left to trade. The rescue nearly costs the SecUnit everything - it takes catastrophic damage destroying the Combat SecUnit sent after them, and what survives has to be rebuilt during the trip out. Pin-Lee, Ratthi and Gurathin get everyone onto a transport bound for Preservation. Aboard, the humans treat the SecUnit as one of them, and Mensah, dealing with the aftereffects of being held hostage, makes clear that she holds its contract only as a legal shield and that its choices are its own. The SecUnit, which has spent three books running from exactly this, admits it does not want to leave. It goes with them to Preservation Station, where it has no legal category, no fixed job description, and a great many people who would like to talk to it about its feelings. The immediate threat is over; what is unresolved is what a free construct is supposed to do with itself, and whether it can live among people who like it.
recaps.in_short: Carrying evidence of GrayCris's illegal salvage back to Preservation, the SecUnit learns from the newsfeeds that Dr. Mensah has been taken hostage by the company and is being held at TranRollinHyfa, a corporate station. It diverts there, works its way past scans built to catch constructs, and finds Pin-Lee, Ratthi and Gurathin already attempting a legal rescue that is going nowhere. Working with them, it locates Mensah, gets her out of GrayCris's custody, and turns the extraction into a running fight when station security is turned against them. GrayCris, financially ruined by the arbitration, throws combat bots and a military-grade Combat SecUnit at them; the SecUnit destroys it and is nearly destroyed in return. The group escapes on a transport bound for Preservation, the hostage plan collapses, and the SecUnit is rebuilt on the way out. Mensah, recovering from her captivity, tells it plainly that it is a person and that the contract she holds exists only to shield it. For the first time the SecUnit chooses company, and goes with them instead of vanishing.

recaps.text: Previously: the SecUnit hacked its own governor module, saved a Preservation survey team from GrayCris, a company that was killing witnesses to its illegal alien remnant salvage, and then left rather than accept Dr. Mensah's offer of a home. Traveling alone, it learned the truth behind the massacre in its deleted memory, made a friend of ART, the bot pilot of a research transport, and then went to the abandoned station at Milu, where it gathered hard evidence of what GrayCris had been doing and where a small trusting bot called Miki was destroyed. Mensah has been fighting GrayCris in arbitration ever since the survey contract ended, and the company has been losing badly. The SecUnit is on its way back toward Preservation with the evidence, intending to hand it over in person rather than send it, having concluded that a cornered GrayCris will come after her directly.

Stopping at a corporate transit station on the way back, the SecUnit finds the newsfeeds carrying a story it was not expecting: Dr. Mensah has disappeared, and the official account of it does not hold together. GrayCris, ruined by the arbitration and desperate for something to trade with, has taken her and is holding her at TranRollinHyfa, a company station where security answers to whoever is paying. The SecUnit changes course. Getting onto the station means passing scans designed to catch exactly what it is, so it works its way in on falsified permissions and a fabricated employer, keeping its weapons and its capabilities out of sight. Once there it discovers that it is not the only rescue attempt in progress: Pin-Lee, Ratthi and Gurathin are already on the station trying to do it through lawyers, money and official channels, and they are being watched.

The SecUnit makes contact with the humans from the old survey team, who are relieved and far too pleased to see it. Together they plan an extraction: the lawyers keep the official channels loud and visible while the SecUnit goes after Mensah directly, using station systems, hacked drones and its own ability to walk through a facility as a piece of equipment nobody looks at twice. It reaches her, alive and held by GrayCris's people, and gets her out of confinement. The company's security works out what has happened almost immediately, and the station stops being somewhere they can leave quietly. Mensah, exhausted and drugged, is the priority; the SecUnit's own condition is a secondary concern to everyone except her.

The escape becomes a running fight across the station. GrayCris commits what it has left, including combat bots and a military-grade Combat SecUnit that outclasses the SecUnit in every measurable way. The SecUnit destroys it, at the cost of catastrophic damage to itself; what remains of it has to be rebuilt aboard the transport out. GrayCris's attempt to use Mensah as leverage collapses, its operation on the station is exposed, and the survivors reach a ship bound for Preservation. On the way, Mensah, dealing with the aftermath of her own captivity, makes plain that the SecUnit is a person with a choice and that the contract she holds over it is only a shield. Rebuilt and still unsure what it wants to be, the SecUnit chooses, for now, to go with them to Preservation rather than disappear again.

characters.description: A young man living with his parents in a city sliding toward civil war. He works at an advertising agency and attends an evening class, where he meets Nadia. Thoughtful, courteous, and attached to his family and religious practice, he is drawn to Nadia's independence even when it unsettles him.
characters.name: Saeed

characters.description: A young woman who lives alone, works for an insurance company, and wears a concealing black robe partly to discourage unwanted attention rather than as an expression of faith. Direct, self-contained, and willing to defy social expectations, she begins seeing Saeed as their city grows more dangerous.
characters.name: Nadia

characters.description: Saeed's gentle, educated father, a university professor whose routines and memories tie him closely to the city. He welcomes Nadia into the family home when conditions deteriorate.
characters.name: Saeed's father

characters.description: Saeed's affectionate mother, who shares a long, companionable marriage with his father and worries about her son's safety as violence spreads through the city.
characters.name: Saeed's mother

characters.description: A secretive man who, for a high fee, arranges access to one of the mysterious doors said to carry people instantly to distant countries. Nadia and Saeed must decide whether his promised route is genuine.
characters.name: The agent

characters.description: A young volunteer on Mykonos who befriends Nadia amid the migrant camp. Her local knowledge and sympathy offer Nadia and Saeed a possible route away from the island.
characters.name: The Mykonos girl

characters.description: An elderly religious leader whom Saeed encounters among London's displaced communities. His group gives Saeed fellowship and a way to preserve faith and continuity while living far from home.
characters.name: The preacher

characters.description: The preacher's warm, capable daughter, active in the religious community that attracts Saeed. She shares his concern for migrants and becomes an increasingly important companion to him.
characters.name: The preacher's daughter

characters.description: A woman in Marin who makes music and works alongside Nadia in the food cooperative. She belongs to the new network of friends through which Nadia builds a life independent of Saeed.
characters.name: The musician

recaps.ending: In Marin, Nadia and Saeed finally acknowledge that the love which carried them out of their city no longer fits the people they have become. They separate gently. Saeed grows close to the preacher's daughter and remains connected to faith and migrant service, while Nadia stays with the cooperative and pursues relationships and work on her own terms. The narrative then moves fifty years ahead. Nadia returns to their transformed home city and meets Saeed in a café. Both have lived long lives apart. They remember their youth without attempting to restore it, and Saeed suggests that they might someday visit the Chilean desert to see the stars. They part with the possibility left open, their reunion affirming the importance of their shared past while accepting that migration, time, and choice have carried them into different futures.
recaps.in_short: In a city falling into civil war, reserved Saeed and fiercely independent Nadia fall in love. As militants seize control and Saeed's mother is killed, the couple use a mysterious door that transports them to Mykonos, joining a worldwide movement of refugees through portals that ignore borders. They later pass to London, where migrants occupy an empty mansion and face violent hostility before a labor-and-housing settlement forms. Moving again to Marin, California, they discover that exile has changed them differently: Saeed seeks faith, community, and cultural continuity, while Nadia embraces new work, friendships, and relationships. They separate with affection rather than betrayal. Fifty years later they meet in their old city, now peaceful and altered, and recall who they were together. Their tentative plan to see the stars leaves them connected by memory even after their lives have diverged.

recaps.text: In an unnamed city where armed conflict is becoming part of daily life, Saeed notices Nadia in an evening class and invites her for coffee. He is a gentle young advertising worker who lives with his parents and retains a quiet religious faith. Nadia is more independent: she has left her family, supports herself through insurance work, rides a motorcycle, and uses her black robe as protection from intrusive men. Their first meetings are cautious but charged with interest. Checkpoints, surveillance, and distant explosions make ordinary courtship increasingly difficult, while rumors spread of dark doors through which people can emerge in faraway places. Saeed and Nadia become lovers, although their different beliefs and temperaments are already visible. Their private attachment grows at the same time that public space in the city is shrinking under violence.

The conflict reaches deeper into Saeed and Nadia's lives. Militants take territory, communications fail, and movement through the city becomes perilous. After Saeed's mother is killed by a stray bullet, Nadia moves into the family home and shares the grief of Saeed and his father. The stories about doors prove true: portals are opening across the world, allowing people to step from one country into another. Nadia contacts an agent who secures them access to one. Saeed wants his father to come, but the older man chooses to remain near his wife's grave and asks Nadia to stay with his son. With no safe future left in the city, the couple pass through the guarded portal together and emerge on the Greek island of Mykonos.

Nadia and Saeed pass through a guarded door and emerge on the Greek island of Mykonos. Their sudden journey leaves them among thousands of other displaced people living in a makeshift camp, with little food, shelter, or certainty. The island is strained but not wholly hostile, and Nadia befriends a local volunteer who helps them learn of another usable door. The couple's bond remains a source of safety, but exile sharpens their differences: Saeed turns toward prayer and fellow countrymen, while Nadia is more willing to form connections across cultures and adapt to unfamiliar surroundings. Helped by the young woman Nadia met, they reach a portal leading away from the island and step through into a wealthy house in London.

In London, Nadia and Saeed join migrants occupying a grand empty house. Rooms and resources are divided among groups from many places, and the building becomes a crowded new community. Outside, established residents demand that the newcomers be removed. Hostility escalates, utilities are cut, and armed forces surround migrant districts, raising the prospect of mass violence. The assault is ultimately halted. A political compromise begins replacing expulsion with organized labor: migrants work on infrastructure and new housing in exchange for wages and a place in planned settlements around the city. Nadia and Saeed move from the mansion to a worker camp in the London halo, alive and temporarily secure. Their different responses to displacement are becoming more visible, and the shared purpose that sustained their escape is weakening.

The London building project offers routine and the promise of a small home, but Nadia and Saeed's intimacy continues to fade. Saeed spends more time with the preacher's community and his daughter; Nadia seeks spaces where origins matter less. They eventually take another door, this time to Marin, California. There they live among migrants in a landscape of improvised dwellings and shifting communities. Nadia works at a food cooperative and forms friendships with her coworkers, including a musician, while Saeed deepens his involvement with religious service and grows close to the preacher's daughter. Neither is openly cruel to the other, yet each increasingly represents a past the other cannot inhabit. They understand that surviving the same journey has not ensured a shared destination.

Nadia and Saeed bring their relationship to a gentle end, recognizing that affection and gratitude remain even though desire and direction have changed. Nadia continues her independent life and relationships in Marin; Saeed builds a future shaped by faith, service, and his closeness to the preacher's daughter. Decades pass. Fifty years after leaving, Nadia visits the city of their youth, which has survived and changed beyond recognition. She and Saeed meet in a café as elderly people and talk about their families, their separate lives, and the time they shared. Saeed recalls his youthful wish to show her the stars above the Chilean desert and suggests that they might still go. They make no firm promise. Their meeting closes the story on recognition rather than reunion: they cannot return to their former selves, but neither distance nor time has erased what they once meant to each other.
